entries.text: Read the error bottom-up: the last line of a Python traceback or the first `error[E...]` of a Rust build names the real problem; the frames above show where. Quote that line back and fix that first.

ModuleNotFoundError / cannot find crate / module not found: the dependency is not installed in the environment you are running. Check `which python`/`node -v`, activate the venv, reinstall from requirements/Cargo.toml/package.json.
Reproduce before fixing: find the smallest input and command that triggers the bug, confirm it fails every time, then change one thing at a time and re-run.
Connection refused = nothing is listening on that host:port (service not started or wrong port). Timeout = host unreachable or firewall. 401/403 = auth or permissions, not networking.
Browser shows stale code: hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R), check the Network tab for the file actually served and its response, and look at the Console for the first red error.
Works on one machine, not another: compare versions (python --version, node -v, rustc -V), environment variables, file paths (absolute vs relative, ~ expansion), and line endings/permissions.
Print/log the actual values at the failing point (type and repr, not just the value) before theorising; most bugs are a wrong assumption about data shape, None/null, or an off-by-one.
